At the upper limit t = ε, the first piece ∫₂^{2+ε} contains the term ln t, which diverges to −∞ at the lower limit t = 0. Since the integrand is positive, the integral is +∞ for every ε > 0.

The second piece, over [3−ε, 3], has a bounded continuous integrand and tends to 0. The sum is therefore +∞ for every ε, so the limit is +∞, not 1.
